speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent; could you tell me how long you've been experiencing these fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss? Also, have you noticed any fever or changes in your bowel habits along with the abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms sound concerning, so I need to ask if you have had any recent travel, exposure to sick contacts, or a history of tuberculosis? Also, have you experienced any unexplained fevers or noticed any lumps in other areas of your body besides the neck?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any family history of cancer or lymphoma, and have you experienced any recent fevers or itching? REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan findings indicate massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Abdominal examination reveals slight distension, dullness over the left lower quadrant, and splenomegaly. Blood work shows elevated White Blood Cell count, slightly decreased Hemoglobin, and elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase. Biopsy of the cervical lymph node confirms lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the CD20-positive biopsy and systemic involvement, I suspect a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or recent infections like EBV, and have you noticed any skin rashes or bleeding? DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
